narrative:
The model estimates a 58% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile that stood out compared with employees the system expects to stay.

Your relatively short overall career experience of 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Most employees the model believes will stay have either 6-10 years or more than 11 years of total experience, so your early-career stage signals higher turnover risk to the system.

The second most influential factor was your monthly salary in the 6k-10k SAR range. While this is the most common salary bracket among those predicted to stay, the model still interpreted it as increasing the likelihood of departure when combined with your other characteristics.

Third, the model noted that you find it difficult to get involved in decision-making and have your opinions heard at work. This stands out because only 10% of employees predicted to stay describe their job engagement this way; the large majority experience it as medium or easy.

Taken together, these three elements outweighed many positive signals such as your lack of overtime and your sector. The organization should consider discussing ways to accelerate your involvement in meaningful decisions and explore clearer paths for faster career progression. You may want to reflect on whether greater responsibility and recognition would increase your commitment to staying.
